description: Discovery hypothesis: small independent medical-practice staff may spend avoidable effort finding payer documentation requirements and tracking non-drug prior authorizations. CMS recognizes a broader prior-authorization burden; the small-practice segment remains unverified.
customer_segment: Hypothesized segment: US small independent practices dealing with affected payers and non-drug medical items/services. No size-specific sample.
geography: United States; payer scope and drug exclusions matter.
context: Administrative work before an authorized medical item/service; no patient information was collected.

evidence.text: CMS describes its rule as reducing prior-authorization burden and specifies APIs for covered items/services, documentation requirements, requests and responses.
The fact sheet specifies denial reasons and describes decision timeframes with payer exclusions.

alternatives: Existing payer channels and practice workflows; CMS explicitly discusses portal, fax, email, mail and phone for denial communication.
Payer APIs described by CMS; EHR/vendor adoption and real availability were not tested.

contradictory_evidence.text: CMS describes operational requirements generally starting in 2026 and API requirements generally starting in 2027: public infrastructure and incumbent adoption may reduce a new entrant's differentiation.
The rule described excludes drugs and does not cover every US payer; a universal workflow claim would overreach.

uncertainty: No small-practice interviews, measured staff time, payer implementation verification or willingness-to-pay evidence. Current regulatory developments after this fact sheet were not exhaustively checked. Clinical integrations and privacy obligations could make a solo-founder MVP difficult.
open_questions: Which documentation/response-tracking gaps remain after current EHR and payer integrations in a narrowly defined specialty?
What later changes affect the 2024 rule and actual 2026/2027 implementation?
next_actions: Check current CMS updates and representative payer/EHR public implementation documentation before any technical opportunity assessment.
Find independent first-hand small-practice evidence; do not treat regulatory intent as a quantified pain estimate.
title: Prior-authorization requirements and response tracking in medical practices

history.reason: Initial public-source discovery for issue #4; no customer interviews or commercial validation.
